issues.legal_issue: A constitutional supervisory challenge should not be entertained when an appeal is available against an order of a specialized debt-recovery tribunal.
material_facts: A bank brought a debt-recovery suit against a principal debtor and guarantors, and the suit was transferred to a specialized debt-recovery tribunal.
The tribunal decreed the claim and directed that mortgaged property be sold as part of recovery proceedings.
A guarantor challenged the tribunal’s direction under constitutional supervisory jurisdiction, arguing that the tribunal lacked territorial jurisdiction over the mortgaged property.
The tribunal’s order was appealable under the statutory appeal process.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have entertained the supervisory petition and should have directed the guarantor to use the statutory appeal process. The High Court’s order was set aside, without deciding whether the tribunal’s direction was correct.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 provides an appeal from tribunal orders. The Act establishes a special, expedited procedure for debt recovery, including an appellate hierarchy; that procedure should not be derailed by recourse to Articles 226 or 227 of the Constitution when an alternative appeal is available. Although constitutional jurisdiction exists, judicial prudence calls for refraining from its exercise in those circumstances. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.debt_recovery_proceeding: A bank or financial institution pursued recovery of a debt through a specialized tribunal.
predicates.tribunal_order_appealable: The challenged tribunal order could be appealed through the governing statutory process.
predicates.constitutional_supervisory_challenge: A party challenged the tribunal’s order by invoking a higher court’s constitutional supervisory jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a party brings a constitutional supervisory challenge to an appealable order made in a specialized debt-recovery proceeding, the challenge is not entertained and the statutory appeal is pursued.
